whatAre.title: What are shrink wrap covers?
whatAre.body: Our made-to-measure shrink wrap covers are made from durable UV-stabilized polyethylene (PE/LDPE). The typical thickness is 150–200 µm, which provides a clean, rigid surface and excellent protection for winter storage and transport. The cover is heat-shrunk into place with heat treatment (heat gun/gas burner), tightening closely to the hull shapes without wrinkling or excess material.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about shrink wrap covers

items.q: How much does boat shrink wrapping cost?
items.a: The price depends on the size and model of the boat. Example prices for made-to-measure shrink wrap covers: Buster L €230.80, Targa 23.1 €351 and Axopar 28 €358.80. On-site shrink wrapping in the Helsinki Capital Region costs €45 per meter (VAT 0%) for console boats under 10 m. Ask for a quote for larger boats and group pricing for multiple boats.

items.q: What is a shrink wrap cover and how does it differ from traditional shrink wrapping?
items.a: A shrink wrap cover is a cover sized in advance to the boat's model or measurements. It is lifted over the boat and heat-shrunk tight. A traditional roll of shrink film weighs about 50 kg, is laborious to install and leaves a lot of offcuts. A ready-made cover means less plastic and faster installation.

items.q: What material are the shrink wrap covers made of?
items.a: The covers are made from durable UV-stabilized polyethylene (PE/LDPE) with a typical thickness of 150–200 µm. The cover keeps the boat clean and protects it from rain, ice and sea salt.

items.q: How long does it take to install a shrink wrap cover?
items.a: The cover is placed over the boat and shrunk with a heat gun or gas burner. For example, an Axopar 28 was wrapped by two people in 45 minutes.

items.q: How do I order a shrink wrap cover for my boat?
items.a: Send the boat model, measurements or drawings using the contact form, by WhatsApp to +358 400 283 123 or by email to jari@kelmutus.fi. We will send you a quote and make the cover to your boat's measurements.

items.q: Do you deliver across Finland, and is on-site installation available?
items.a: Shrink wrap covers are delivered across Finland. On-site shrink wrapping is available in the Helsinki Capital Region, and outside it for an additional fee.

items.q: Does a shrink-wrapped boat need ventilation during winter storage?
items.a: Yes. Ventilation vents and an inspection window are available as accessories for the cover. During winter storage, leave hatches and doors slightly open and make sure the shrink wrap has ventilation openings.

items.q: Can you shrink wrap things other than boats?
items.a: Yes. We also shrink wrap cars, industrial machinery and equipment, buildings and special items, either with a made-to-measure cover or on site.

meta.title: Boat winter storage: guide and checklist | Kelmutus.fi
meta.description: Boat winter storage step by step: cleaning and drying, engine and fuel, batteries, ventilation and protecting the boat with shrink wrap. Read the checklist.

talvisailytys.title: Boat winter storage guide
talvisailytys.intro: Careful preparation protects your boat from moisture, mold and frost damage over the winter. Go through this checklist before the boat is laid up for the season.

cta.title: Need help with winter storage for your boat?
cta.body: We make a made-to-measure shrink wrap cover for your boat, shrink wrap it on site in the Helsinki Capital Region and can also take care of winter service.

cleanSurfaces.label: Clean surfaces:
cleanSurfaces.text: Wash the boat’s interior (cabinets, surfaces) with mild soapy water or diluted vinegar water.

removeMoisture.label: Remove moisture:
removeMoisture.text: Ventilate the boat thoroughly. Make sure there is no water left in hoses, the fridge, or other recesses.

dryThoroughly.label: Dry thoroughly:
dryThoroughly.text: Let all surfaces dry completely, as moisture promotes mold growth.

items.dehumidifier: Use moisture absorbers, e.g. an Absodry dehumidifier from Motonet.

fillTank.label: Fill the tank:
fillTank.text: Keep the fuel tank full to prevent condensation.

protectEngine.label: Protect the engine:
protectEngine.text: Use antifreeze (glycol) or another freeze protection product according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

service.label: Service:
service.text: Change oils and filters, and empty or replace the water separator filter.

removeSensitive.label: Remove moisture-sensitive items:
removeSensitive.text: Take out textiles, tools, electronics and other loose items.

storeBatteries.label: Store batteries properly:
storeBatteries.text: Disconnect the batteries and store them in a dry, warm place for the winter.

washRopes.label: Wash ropes:
washRopes.text: Rinse ropes with fresh water and dry them well before storage.

shrinkWrap.label: Shrink-wrap the boat:
shrinkWrap.text: A made-to-measure shrink wrap cover protects the boat from dirt, rain, ice and sea salt.

ventilation.label: Ensure ventilation:
ventilation.text: Leave hatches and doors slightly open, and make sure there are ventilation openings in the shrink wrap.

emptyBilge.label: Empty the bilge:
emptyBilge.text: Open the drain plug and check that no water remains in the bilge. If needed, remove the rest with a wet vacuum. Also check that the bilge pump works.

drainWaterSystems.label: Drain water systems:
drainWaterSystems.text: Drain the fresh water system and pour antifreeze into the toilet bowl.

items.finalNote: Your boat is now ready for spring — you can safely start planning the routes for the next season ☺
